samples.summary: New timeout classification in startCallbackServer (system-error vs user-error LoginError) has no test
samples.evidence: The diff adds a branch in the 30s timeout of `startCallbackServer`: when `sawUnboundCallback` is true it rejects with `LoginError(EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR, 'Login callback arrived without the expected nonce …')`, otherwise `LoginError(EXIT_USER_ERROR, 'Login timed out …')`. packages/cli/test/login.test.ts exercises the 403 rejection path (`refuses a callback with a mismatched nonce`, `refuses a callback with no nonce at all`) but always follows it with a successful callback, so the timeout is never reached and neither the message nor the 1-vs-2 exit class is asserted. Grep for `timed out`, `sawUnbound`, `useFakeTimers` across packages/cli finds matches only in src/commands/login.ts, never in test/. This is precisely the exit-contract behavior the PR exists to introduce.

samples.summary: No test asserts the CLI actually sends `nonce=` on the OAuth URL
samples.evidence: `runLogin` builds `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}&nonce=${encodeURIComponent(nonce)}` and generates the nonce it later binds the callback to, but `runLogin` is not exported and login.test.ts only drives `startCallbackServer`, `fetchLoginSession`, `nonceMatches` and `classifyLoginFailure`. A grep for `mode=cli` in packages/cli finds only the source line; nothing pins that the nonce handed to the callback server is the same one sent to the server, which is the whole binding.

samples.summary: Backend: the nonce-less redirect branch (`nonceParam = ''`) is not pinned by any test
samples.evidence: The controller now appends `&nonce=…` only when `state.nonce` exists. The new spec case (`echoes the CLI nonce…`, auth.controller.spec.ts:214) covers the present branch, but the pre-existing case at auth.controller.spec.ts:189 asserts only `/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:9876\/callback\?code=.+/`, which matches whether or not a stray `nonce=` is appended. So a regression that emitted e.g. `&nonce=undefined` for a nonce-less (older) CLI would pass the suite.

samples.summary: files download's switch to exitCodeForStatus is untested; the only failure test (404) passes identically before and after
samples.evidence: download.ts now returns `exitCodeForStatus(res.status)` instead of a hardcoded 1. packages/cli/test/files-download.test.ts:129-142 is the only failure test and uses status 404 expecting exitCode 1 — the same value the old hardcoded branch produced, so nothing in the suite would fail if the new call were reverted. The sibling upload test was updated to a 500/exit-2 case; download has no 401/5xx case.

samples.summary: The `data:` early-return in the new SSRF gate has no test
samples.evidence: `assertFetchableImageUrl` returns early for `data:` URLs (and `FETCHABLE_SCHEMES` includes `data:`), i.e. inline images are deliberately allowed through the gate. The new `createImageFetcher SSRF gate` suite in packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts tests `file:` and `blob:` refusals, internal addresses/hosts, DNS failures and redirects, but no case asserts a `data:` src is still fetched — a regression that blocked inline images would go unnoticed.
searchedFor: read the image-fetcher.test.ts hunk in the diff

samples.summary: Weak assertions in the export exit-code cases: the file-write claim is unasserted and the 404 cases pass for any incidental failure
samples.evidence: `it('exits 2 on a 401 without writing the file')` asserts only `process.exitCode === 2`; nothing stubs or observes the filesystem, so the 'without writing the file' claim is untested. Likewise `exits 1 on a 404` only checks exit code 1, which is also the code produced by any unrelated thrown error routed through `outputError` (e.g. a format-detection failure), so those cases cannot distinguish the intended branch from an incidental one.

finding.summary: New timeout classification in startCallbackServer (system-error vs user-error LoginError) has no test
finding.evidence: The diff adds a branch in the 30s timeout of `startCallbackServer`: when `sawUnboundCallback` is true it rejects with `LoginError(EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR, 'Login callback arrived without the expected nonce …')`, otherwise `LoginError(EXIT_USER_ERROR, 'Login timed out …')`. packages/cli/test/login.test.ts exercises the 403 rejection path (`refuses a callback with a mismatched nonce`, `refuses a callback with no nonce at all`) but always follows it with a successful callback, so the timeout is never reached and neither the message nor the 1-vs-2 exit class is asserted. Grep for `timed out`, `sawUnbound`, `useFakeTimers` across packages/cli finds matches only in src/commands/login.ts, never in test/. This is precisely the exit-contract behavior the PR exists to introduce.

verdict.reason: The claimed branch is real: login.ts:362-381 rejects the callback promise with LoginError(EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR, 'Login callback arrived without the expected nonce …') when sawUnboundCallback (set at login.ts:308) is true, otherwise LoginError(EXIT_USER_ERROR, 'Login timed out …'). No test exercises it. The nonce-rejection tests (login.test.ts:146-173) do set sawUnboundCallback via 403 responses, but each then sends a valid callback and asserts waitForCallback() RESOLVES to 'good-code', and the finally block calls srv.close(), which clearTimeout()s the 30s timer (login.ts:396-399) — so the timeout callback never runs and neither the message nor the exit class is asserted. Searching wide for a counterexample: startCallbackServer/waitForCallback appear only in login.ts and login.test.ts; the literal messages appear only in login.ts, docs/design/cli.md and an unrelated backend guard message; no fake timers anywhere in packages/cli/test (only match for 'timeout' is a vitest per-test timeout in docs-export.test.ts:215); command-exit-codes.test.ts covers API commands, not the login timeout; the classifyLoginFailure tests (login.test.ts:200-218) hand-construct LoginError and pass regardless of which timeout arm is taken. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a user-visible exit-contract behavior (documented in docs/design/cli.md:192,904) with no meaningful test — major.

finding.summary: API-key endpoints rerouted through `send()` (401 refresh-and-retry, encoded id) with no test exercising HttpClient
finding.evidence: `listApiKeys`/`createApiKey`/`revokeApiKey` were rewritten to go through the private `send()` helper, whose documented purpose is that "a refreshable session is never reported as an auth failure just because of which base a call used" (http-client.ts:105-111), plus `encodeURIComponent(id)` on revoke. Nothing tests this: the only HttpClient test in the repo is docs-content.test.ts:301-337 (a single 409 passthrough on getDocContent); grep for `apiKey|refreshSession|refresh` across packages/cli/test finds no refresh-retry test at all. The new command-exit-codes.test.ts replaces the whole client with a Proxy stub (`vi.mock('../src/commands/root.js')`, lines 17-35), so `send()` — including the URL construction and the refresh path it now shares with api-keys — is mocked away entirely.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test exercises HttpClient's API-key endpoints going through send() (401 refresh-and-retry, encoded revoke id). A dedicated file packages/cli/test/http-client.test.ts exists and does exactly that: it imports the real HttpClient (line 5), stubs only globalThis.fetch (lines 42-57), and asserts (a) the management-base URL and auth header on listApiKeys (76-88), (b) percent-encoding of the revoke id -> /api-keys/a%2Fb%20c with DELETE (90-98), (c) the full 401 -> /auth/refresh -> retry sequence with the refreshed Bearer token (100-129), (d) refreshed tokens persisted to the real session file (131-165), (e) the SESSION_EXPIRED envelope when refresh is rejected (167-186), (f) no retry under api-key auth (188-195), and (g) NETWORK_ERROR/SystemError classification via fetchOrThrow (197-209). Real send()/sendJson()/refreshSession() code paths run — nothing under test is mocked. vitest.config.ts include 'test/**/*.test.ts' confirms the file is collected. The reviewer's stated premise ("the only HttpClient test in the repo is docs-content.test.ts") is factually wrong.
